html:
The Wandjiwalgu were an Aboriginal Australian people of far western New South Wales, west of the Darling River and north of Menindee. Their speech was a dialect of Paakantyi, the language of the Barkindji.

Little is recorded of them as a separate group. Their neighbours included the Bandjigali, another Paakantyi group, the Wiljali and the Paaruntyi. Sheep stations took the country in the 1860s.
